sub_graphs.title: Prague: Jump Destination Validation
sub_graphs.description: Models the process of identifying valid jump destinations in EVM bytecode

nodes.label: Bytecode Received for Analysis
nodes.description: EVM bytecode has been provided for jump destination analysis

nodes.label: Initialize Jump Destinations Set
nodes.description: Create empty set to store valid jump positions

nodes.label: PC at Opcode Position
nodes.description: Program counter is positioned at an opcode to analyze

nodes.label: Read Opcode at PC
nodes.description: Read the opcode byte at current program counter position

nodes.label: Check if JUMPDEST
nodes.description: Compare opcode against 0x5B (JUMPDEST)

nodes.label: Add Position to Valid Set
nodes.description: Add current PC position to valid_jump_destinations set

nodes.label: Check if PUSH Opcode
nodes.description: Determine if opcode is PUSH1-PUSH32 (0x60-0x7F)

nodes.label: Compute PUSH Data Size
nodes.description: Calculate push data size as (opcode - 0x60 + 1)

nodes.label: Advance PC Past PUSH Data
nodes.description: Skip over PUSH data bytes that are not valid jump targets

nodes.label: Advance PC by One
nodes.description: Move program counter to next opcode

nodes.label: Jump Analysis Complete
nodes.description: All valid jump destinations have been identified

nodes.label: Unknown Opcode Encountered
nodes.description: An undefined opcode is encountered during bytecode analysis

nodes.label: Skip Invalid Opcode
nodes.description: Treat unknown opcode as single-byte instruction and continue

nodes.description: Analysis proceeds past invalid opcode without error

ambiguities.text: The specification does not explicitly state whether the valid_jump_destinations set is cached or recomputed for each call
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume the set is computed once per code execution context and reused for the duration of that call frame.

ambiguities.text: The phrase 'invalid opcodes' is used without defining which opcodes are considered invalid
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume any opcode not defined in the current fork's instruction set is invalid (opcodes > 0xFF or undefined in opcode table).

implicit_assumptions.description: The bytecode being analyzed is immutable and cannot change during analysis or between analysis and execution
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Mutable bytecode could cause the pre-computed jump destinations to become invalid, allowing jumps to non-JUMPDEST locations

implicit_assumptions.description: PUSH data bytes are correctly interpreted as data and not opcodes, regardless of their byte value
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: If PUSH data containing 0x5B is misinterpreted as JUMPDEST, it could create exploitable jump targets within data

implicit_assumptions.description: The bytecode length does not exceed memory limits during analysis
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Extremely large bytecode could cause out-of-memory conditions during jump destination analysis
